claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The homogenized alloy exhibits strong-yet-brittle behavior.
Its FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent and prone to interfacial cracking.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus will transform the dual-phase lamellae into a hierarchical microstructure with coherent interfaces.
The HPHT treatment refines the microstructure.
Coherent interfaces enable preferential dislocation transfer from the softer FCC phase into the harder B2 phase.
Preferential interphase dislocation transfer reduces local stress concentrations.
The hierarchical pattern activates dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and twins during deformation.
These multiple deformation mechanisms accommodate room-temperature plasticity and distribute strain more homogeneously.
HPHT treatment will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to untreated or conventionally processed material.
The treated alloy will attain an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 1150 MPa.
The treated alloy will attain tensile ductility of approximately 36%.
HPHT treatment will change fracture from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed microcracking.
Conventional arc-melted and cast eutectic high-entropy alloys or their homogenized variants exhibit room-temperature brittleness and limited ductility.
The enhanced properties are contingent on treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
Conventional thermomechanical treatments or hot isostatic pressing at lower pressures will not produce similar effects.
Analogous phenomena in similar alloy systems provide prior plausibility for the proposed mechanism and outcomes.
At approximately 35% strain, the treated alloy will show similar geometrically necessary dislocation densities in its FCC and B2 phases.
